databases:
• Access World News
    Access World News is a comprehensive resource that includes a variety of news publications worldwide, as well as titles from the Advocate and Picayune families of newspapers. It is available to LSU students, faculty, and staff.
  • African American Newspapers, 1827-1998
    African American Newspapers provides online access to approximately 270 newspapers from over 35 states, including 15 from Louisiana. It is available to LSU students, faculty, and staff.
  • America's Historical Newspapers
    America's Historical Newspapers provides more than 1,300 titles from all 50 states, including 39 from Louisiana. It is available to LSU students, faculty, and staff.
  • American Prison Newspapers, 1800s-present: Voices from the Inside
    American Prison Newspapers is an open-access database of newspapers published inside US prisons, including 15 from Louisiana between 1940 and the present.
  • Chronicling America: Historic American Newspapers
    The Library of Congress's Chronicling America database, which is available online to everyone, includes 128 Louisiana titles between 1836 and 1922.
  • Google News
    The Google News database, which is available online to everyone, includes 18 New Orleans titles between 1810 and 1923.
  • Louisiana Newspapers on the Louisiana Digital Library
    The Louisiana Digital Library, which is available online to everyone, hosts dozens of active and historical Louisiana newspapers from 1824 to the present.
  • Newspapers.com
    Newspapers.com, a subsidiary of Ancestry.com, provides access to over 460 Louisiana newspapers from 1802 to the present. It is available to LSU students, faculty, and staff, as well as visitors to our reading room.
  • Nineteenth Century U.S. Newspapers
    Nineteenth Century U.S. Newspapers provides access to over 400 US newspapers, including several from Louisiana. It is available to LSU students, faculty, and staff.
